analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the last-updated date (line 3) and adds a documentation paragraph near head line 1293 describing PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup behavior. Per the description, lookup snapshots all of a request's hits before promoting them between two bounded generations. A promotion that rotates the cache therefore cannot turn a later piece in the same lookup into a miss. Token arrays share storage during the snapshot, and the existing admission and byte bounds are unchanged. Batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. The added lines (1293-1298) are in the patch but not in the supplied head text units, which end around line 805. I could therefore not verify the surrounding context or the prefix-cache scope wording on the head side. The supplied patch excerpt is complete.

Security relevance: the token-piece cache is described as scoped per prefix-cache scope, which relates to T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache and TTFT oracle, SEC-035). The doc change describes no new cross-scope sharing, no new at-rest artifact, no change to TTL, disk budget, HMAC naming or scope derivation, and no new endpoints or trust boundaries. The snapshot-before-promote logic is a correctness and determinism fix. It could slightly reduce timing variance from a rotation-induced miss, and it does not enlarge the cross-tenant surface. The remaining source-level question is whether the actual code in PromptPieceTokenStore keeps the scope partitioning intact, and whether shared token-array storage can leak across scopes. That code was not supplied, and the documentation alone gives no evidence of a regression. A later pass with the source should confirm that the scope key still partitions both generations. I found no concrete security regression in the supplied evidence.
